Action: Every bkit workflow runs a `bkit:gate*` script, so a missing link fails the whole gate. Add `bkit:lint:prose`, `bkit:slop:delta`, `build`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, `typecheck` to package.json (`.bkit/templates.md` lists the tool scripts and the devDeps they need), or edit the `bkit:gate*` scripts to drop what this repo does not have. Gate contents (`.bkit/workflows.md` § Local gate scripts): every gate but `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration-e2e` and `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration-e2e-live` runs on a push or inside `/bkit-build`, so it MUST NOT run tests that need a deployed boundary or remote service; local services (a database in Docker) are fine. --- 3/11 [advisory] test-file-script-missing --- Detect: package.json does not declare `bkit:test:file`, so `/bkit-build` cannot check that each task's tests fail before its code is written. Action: Add `bkit:test:file` to package.json: it runs the ONE test file bkit appends as its argument (repo-relative path) and writes a JUnit report to the path in `$BKIT_TEST_REPORT`. Vitest example: "bkit:test:file": "vitest run --reporter=default --reporter=junit --outputFile.junit=\"$BKIT_TEST_REPORT\"" jest reads a bare path as a regex, so a folder such as `(tabs)` matches no file: pass `--runTestsByPath`. Call the runner directly, not through a task runner that caches results or runs dependent packages first. A monorepo routes the path to the package and config that own it. --- 4/11 [advisory] gate-changed-script-missing --- Detect: package.json does not declare `bkit:gate:changed`, so `/bkit-build` and `/bkit-debug` agents run a whole gate (`bkit:gate:static` or `bkit:gate:static-unit`) after every change instead of checking only what changed. Action: Add `bkit:gate:changed` to package.json. `bkit tests changed` calls it with the changed files as its arguments (repo-relative paths: uncommitted, untracked and committed since the step began; deleted files left out) and never with none. It runs the tests that import those files, the tests that name their paths, and the static checks (lint, format, typecheck) on those files, exiting 0 when clean. Vitest + ESLint example, with `scripts/gate-changed.sh` holding `vitest related --run "$@" && eslint --max-warnings=0 --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern "$@" && prettier --check --ignore-unknown "$@"`: "bkit:gate:changed": "sh scripts/gate-changed.sh" `vitest related` finds only importers; also run the tests that read a changed file by its path (a text search of the test files for each path). The orchestrator's group gate, pre-push and CI still run the whole gates. To keep the whole gate on every change, add `gate-changed-script-missing` to `bkit.advisories.ignore` in package.json. Gate contents (`.bkit/workflows.md` § Local gate scripts): every gate but `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration-e2e` and `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration-e2e-live` runs on a push or inside `/bkit-build`, so it MUST NOT run tests that need a deployed boundary or remote service; local services (a database in Docker) are fine. --- 5/11 [advisory] gh-mcp-token-unset-shell --- Detect: BKIT_GH_TOKEN is not set in the shell environment (undefined). Action: Set BKIT_GH_TOKEN in .bkit/.env (canonical local-secrets file, gitignored), then `direnv allow` and restart your editor so MCP servers pick it up: cp .bkit/.env.example .bkit/.env # if not already done # edit .bkit/.env — set BKIT_GH_TOKEN=<PAT> direnv allow Use a fine-grained PAT when every target repo sits under one owner (Contents, Pull requests, Issues, and Actions read & write, plus organization-scoped Projects read & write if you use board sync); use a classic PAT when one token must span owners (scopes repo / workflow / read:org / project / security_events). Generate at: https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens (fine-grained) or https://github.com/settings/tokens (classic). In cloud sessions (Claude Code web / Cursor Cloud Agents / Codex Cloud) set BKIT_GH_TOKEN in the dashboard env vars instead — repo files are not read for secrets there. --- 6/11 [advisory] tracker-setup-github --- Detect: bkit tracker is configured as `github`. Action: GitHub tracker: the GitHub MCP server authenticates with `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT for one owner, classic PAT across owners) — set it in `.bkit/.env`, then `direnv allow`. Unset → every tracker and PR MCP call fails. The `gh` CLI signs in separately: run `gh auth login` once. Ensure the `github` MCP server is configured in `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`. --- 7/11 [advisory] github-project-board-sync-unconfigured --- Detect: GitHub tracker is active but Projects v2 board status sync is not fully configured: `bkit.tracker.github.project` is empty or absent in package.json. Board sync silently no-ops — workflows never reflect phase on the project board. Action: Board status sync is optional (workflows never gate on it) but invisible when half-configured. All three prerequisites are required: 1. Add the board's URL to package.json, as the browser shows it on the board (`/orgs/<org>/…` for an organization board, `/users/<login>/…` for a personal one; a trailing `/views/<n>` is fine): "bkit": { "tracker": { "github": { "project": "https://github.com/orgs/<org>/projects/<number>" } } } Workflows set the board's Status field by option name: `In progress` when a phase starts, `In review` at hand-off. A board whose Status options are named differently sets `"progress"` and `"review"` beside `"project"` to its own names. 2. Ensure the root `.mcp.json` github server enables the `projects` toolset: "X-MCP-Toolsets": "context,issues,pull_requests,repos,users,projects,actions" 3. The `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` PAT needs Projects read & write (repo scope is not enough): a fine-grained PAT gets it as an organization permission, so it reaches organization boards only; a classic PAT with the `project` scope reaches organization and personal boards. To opt out and silence this advisory, set `bkit.tracker.github.project` to `false` in package.json. --- 8/11 [advisory] cloud-secrets-three-locations --- Detect: The secrets bkit's cloud integration uses must also be set in each cloud location you use. Then run `direnv allow` to auto-export them into your shell. .bkit/.env is gitignored and safe to commit-skip. --- Setup tips --- Things not set up yet, most useful first. For the person: each tip says what goes wrong today and a sentence to ask your agent. For an AI agent: follow each tip's Agent steps unless the person declines it. Silence a tip by adding its id to `bkit.advisories.ignore` in package.json; `bkit-upgrade` cannot be silenced. Full template catalogue: .bkit/templates.md. 1. Give bkit its GitHub token (gh-mcp) You chose GitHub as your tracker, but bkit has no GitHub token, so every attempt to read an issue or open a pull request will fail. Add the token. Why: Choosing GitHub only tells bkit where your issues live. The token is what lets it actually sign in. Without it the setting looks right but nothing works, which is confusing to track down. Ask your agent: "Add my GitHub token as `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` in .bkit/.env, check .mcp.json has the `github` server, then run `direnv allow` and tell me to restart the editor." Agent steps: `.bkit/install.md` § Local env setup. The `github` server entry belongs in `.mcp.json` / `.cursor/mcp.json` (`.bkit/cloud.md` § MCP issue-tracker integration). 2. Create bkit's private settings file (bkit-env) bkit's private settings file (.bkit/.env) is missing or has blank entries, so nothing that needs to sign in can. Create it and fill it in. Why: This one file holds the sign-in tokens every bkit tool reads. It's never shared or committed. Most other tips depend on it, so do this one early. Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/.env.example to .bkit/.env and tell me which values I need to fill in." Agent steps: `.bkit/install.md` § Local env setup. 3. Let agents look code up directly (serena) Agents are finding code by searching for words, which is slower, costs more, and misses things. Set up Serena so they can look code up directly. Why: Serena lets agents look up code the way your editor does ("where is this defined, and what uses it?") instead of guessing from text search and reading whole files. That means fewer accidental changes, fewer rounds of you correcting them, and lower running costs because they read less. It can only look things up, never change your files. Ask your agent: "Run `brew install uv` and `uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent`, copy .bkit/templates/.serena/project.yml to .serena/project.yml and .bkit/templates/scripts/serena/ to scripts/serena/, then add the `serena` server from scripts/serena/bkit-serena.mcp.json to .mcp.json (details: .bkit/templates.md § Serena)." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Serena. 4. Automatic checks on every change (ci-workflow) Nothing checks your changes automatically before they're merged, so broken code can land unnoticed. Add bkit's check workflow. Why: This runs your tests and checks on GitHub every time something changes, and bkit's ship step waits for it to pass before merging. Without it, "shipped" only means "merged", not "checked". Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml to .github/workflows/<the file package.json `bkit.testing.ciWorkflow` names; default bkit-ci.yml>, replace `main` and `{{NODE_VERSION}}` in it with my default branch and Node major version, and add the `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `bkit:lint:prose`, `bkit:slop:delta` and `test` scripts to package.json as listed in .bkit/templates.md § Gate tool scripts." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § CI workflow and § Gate tool scripts. 5. Catch problems before they leave your machine (husky) Mistakes are only caught after changes reach GitHub. Add the local checks so they're caught the moment a change is saved to git. Why: These run the same checks on your own computer, in seconds, whenever a change is committed or pushed. Without them you find out minutes later from a failed build, after the agent has moved on and fixing it costs more. Ask your agent: "Run `pnpm add -D husky`, add `"prepare": "husky"` to the package.json scripts, copy .bkit/templates/.husky/pre-commit and .bkit/templates/.husky/pre-push to .husky/, and run `chmod +x .husky/pre-commit .husky/pre-push`." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Git hooks. 6. Consistent formatting (prettier) There's no shared formatting setup, so reviews fill up with spacing changes that hide the real ones. Add Prettier with bkit's ignore file. Why: Prettier (a code formatter) makes every file follow the same layout. bkit's ignore file stops it reformatting bkit's own files, which would otherwise show up as false changes every time bkit updates. Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/templates/prettierignore.example to .prettierignore first, then run `pnpm add -D prettier` and add `"format:check": "prettier --check ."` to the package.json scripts." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Prettier. 7. Catch junk code (slop-scan) Nothing catches the junk code AI tends to write. Add slop-scan so new junk gets flagged before it's merged. Why: Filler and dead code look fine when you skim a change, so they pile up unnoticed until the codebase is hard to trust. slop-scan flags only new problems, so it won't bury you in old ones. Ask your agent: "Run `pnpm add -D slop-scan`, copy .bkit/templates/slop-scan.config.json to slop-scan.config.json and .bkit/templates/scripts/slop/ to scripts/slop/, and add `"lint:slop": "slop-scan scan ."` and `"bkit:slop:delta": "bkit ci slop"` to the package.json scripts." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § slop-scan. 8. Keep written docs tight (vale) Nothing checks the project's written docs, so they slowly fill with vague, padded wording that agents then have to read. Add Vale. Why: Agents read your docs and instructions on every run. Padded writing costs time and money every time it's read, and vague rules get followed vaguely. Vale (a writing checker) flags it. Ask your agent: "Run `brew install vale`, copy .bkit/templates/.vale.ini to .vale.ini and .bkit/templates/.vale/styles/Bkit/ to .vale/styles/Bkit/, then run `vale sync`." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Vale. 9. Quick tidy-up on commit (lint-staged) The commit check has nothing to run. Add lint-staged so it tidies just the files you're committing. Why: It formats only the handful of files in each change, in about a second. Without it the commit check either does nothing or is slow enough that people start skipping it. Ask your agent: "Run `pnpm add -D lint-staged prettier` and copy .bkit/templates/lintstagedrc.example.json to .lintstagedrc.json." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § lint-staged. 10. Let debugging see real errors (context-fetch) When something breaks, the debug workflow can't see your live error reports or logs, so it has to guess from the code. Connect the services you use. Why: This lets /bkit-debug read the actual errors from your error tracker, hosting and database. Without it the agent works from guesses, and real problems stay hidden because nothing brings in the evidence. Ask your agent: "Copy the blocks for the services this project uses from .bkit/templates/context/ into .agents/context.md, below the `<!-- bkit:end -->` line, then tell me which tokens to add to .bkit/.env." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Context-fetch blocks. 11. Keep passwords the same everywhere (secrets-sync) Your deployment passwords are updated by hand in each service. Add bkit's sync tool so they're set in one place and copied everywhere. Why: The same password usually lives in several places: your hosting, your database, GitHub. When one falls out of step you get "works for me, broken in production", the slowest kind of bug to find. This keeps them matching and proves it without showing any values. Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/templates/scripts/secrets/ to scripts/secrets/, fill in scripts/secrets/bkit-secrets.config.mjs for the services this project uses, then run `node scripts/secrets/bkit-secrets.mjs sync --dry-run`." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Secrets sync. 12. Summarise long sessions earlier (compaction-window) Long sessions only summarise themselves when they're nearly full, so every step re-reads a huge history, and that re-reading is most of what a run costs. Set an earlier summarise point. Why: Each request re-reads the whole session so far. Left at the default, a session grows close to the model's full size before it summarises, and most subagents never summarise at all. An earlier summarise point keeps every request smaller. Caution: Summaries lose some detail. A summarise point set too low can stop agents mid-run. 300,000 tokens is a starting value, not yet checked on a real build. Ask your agent: "Add `"autoCompactWindow": 300000` to .claude/settings.json. For Codex, add `model_auto_compact_token_limit = 300000` at the top of .codex/config.toml, above the first `[section]`." Agent steps: `.bkit/providers.md` § Context compaction. Claude Code: `"autoCompactWindow": 300000` in `.claude/settings.json`. Codex: `model_auto_compact_token_limit = 300000` in `.codex/config.toml`, above the first `[section]` header. 13. Stop loading claude.ai connectors in this project (claude-connectors) Claude Code loads every connector on your claude.ai account in this project (for example email, calendar or file storage) and sends their names with every request, even when unused. If agents here don't use them, switch them off for this project. Why: Every connector's tool names are re-sent on every request, which is the largest part of the starting load you can remove. The connectors keep working in ordinary Claude chats (web and desktop app) and in cloud routines; only Claude Code in this project stops loading them. Ask your agent: "Check whether agents in this project use any claude.ai connectors. If none, add `"disableClaudeAiConnectors": true` to .claude/settings.json." Agent steps: `.bkit/providers.md` § claude.ai connectors. Move anything agents use through a connector onto the project's MCP file first, then set `"disableClaudeAiConnectors": true` in `.claude/settings.json`. 14. Issue forms (issue-forms) Optional: add issue forms so every new issue asks for what the agent reads first. Why: Each workflow starts from the issue. A form for an idea, a well-defined change or a bug asks for the problem, what done looks like, or the steps to reproduce. Without one, issues often arrive as a title and a line, and the agent has to guess. Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/templates/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ to .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ and commit it to the default branch." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Issue forms. 15. A map of the code (graphify) Optional: add graphify to keep an up-to-date map of how your code fits together. Why: With a map, agents check what already exists before building it again. Without one, agents and reviews work out the structure from scratch each time. That's slower, and it's easy to miss how one change ripples into another part of the code. Ask your agent: "Run `uv tool install "graphifyy[sql]"`, copy .bkit/templates/scripts/graphify/ to scripts/graphify/ and .bkit/templates/.graphifyignore to .graphifyignore, then add the graph scripts to package.json as listed in .bkit/templates.md § graphify." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § graphify. 16. Project docs (project-docs) Fill the project docs in waves, because each doc reads facts the earlier ones record. Why: Agents read your architecture, testing and security docs before they plan and build. A doc that is missing or still holds the starter text gives them nothing to go on, so they guess from the code each time. Caution: Ignoring either the missing-doc advisory or the unfilled-doc advisory also silences this tip and the other advisory. Ask your agent: "Fill in my project docs in the order of .bkit/templates.md § Project docs — adoption order: copy each missing starter from .bkit/templates/docs/ to docs/, fill it from the repository, and add its row to .agents/docs.md." Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Project docs — adoption order. 17. Project goals (project-goals) Agents have rules but no goals, so when two options both fit the rules they choose by guesswork. The rules say what is allowed, not what matters most here, so each agent weighs speed, cost and polish its own way. --- 1/11 [advisory] context-fetch-missing ---
Detect: `.agents/context.md` has the bkit-managed block but no `<!-- context-fetch:start [name] --> ... <!-- context-fetch:end -->` block after `<!-- bkit:end -->`. `/bkit-debug` runs every block in that consumer section — with none, no runtime-log artifact is produced.
Action: Copy the blocks of a provider file in `.bkit/templates/context/` (e.g. `bkit-vercel.md`, `bkit-supabase.md`; index in `.bkit/templates.md` § Context-fetch blocks) and paste them after `<!-- bkit:end -->`, then set its env vars. REQUIRED: set the block's non-secret selector (e.g. `VERCEL_SCOPE` / `SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID`) by uncommenting the assignment line at the top of the copied block — committing it there is what makes the block run in headless cloud agents, which never read `.bkit/.env`. For cloud `/bkit-debug`, also set the secret tokens (`VERCEL_TOKEN` / `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`) in your Claude/Cursor dashboard (or GitHub Actions secrets) and authenticate non-interactively (env tokens, never `vercel login`). Each block self-gates (missing CLI / token => a `[context-fetch:<name>] skipped — …` stderr breadcrumb, not an error), so enable only the sources you use; add your own block for any other log backend (`gcloud` / `aws` / `datadog`). Keep blocks read-only and idempotent — the agent customises severity / freshness / limit / target environment (e.g. Vercel preview vs production) at run-time.

--- 2/11 [advisory] gate-missing-called-scripts ---
Detect: The bkit:gate scripts call scripts package.json does not declare: `bkit:lint:prose`, `bkit:slop:delta`, `build`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, `typecheck`.
Action: Every bkit workflow runs a `bkit:gate*` script, so a missing link fails the whole gate. Add `bkit:lint:prose`, `bkit:slop:delta`, `build`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, `typecheck` to package.json (`.bkit/templates.md` lists the tool scripts and the devDeps they need), or edit the `bkit:gate*` scripts to drop what this repo does not have.

Gate contents (`.bkit/workflows.md` § Local gate scripts): every gate but `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration-e2e` and `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration-e2e-live` runs on a push or inside `/bkit-build`, so it MUST NOT run tests that need a deployed boundary or remote service; local services (a database in Docker) are fine.

--- 3/11 [advisory] test-file-script-missing ---
Detect: package.json does not declare `bkit:test:file`, so `/bkit-build` cannot check that each task's tests fail before its code is written.
Action: Add `bkit:test:file` to package.json: it runs the ONE test file bkit appends as its argument (repo-relative path) and writes a JUnit report to the path in `$BKIT_TEST_REPORT`. Vitest example:

    "bkit:test:file": "vitest run --reporter=default --reporter=junit --outputFile.junit=\"$BKIT_TEST_REPORT\""

jest reads a bare path as a regex, so a folder such as `(tabs)` matches no file: pass `--runTestsByPath`. Call the runner directly, not through a task runner that caches results or runs dependent packages first. A monorepo routes the path to the package and config that own it.

--- 4/11 [advisory] gate-changed-script-missing ---
Detect: package.json does not declare `bkit:gate:changed`, so `/bkit-build` and `/bkit-debug` agents run a whole gate (`bkit:gate:static` or `bkit:gate:static-unit`) after every change instead of checking only what changed.
Action: Add `bkit:gate:changed` to package.json. `bkit tests changed` calls it with the changed files as its arguments (repo-relative paths: uncommitted, untracked and committed since the step began; deleted files left out) and never with none. It runs the tests that import those files, the tests that name their paths, and the static checks (lint, format, typecheck) on those files, exiting 0 when clean. Vitest + ESLint example, with `scripts/gate-changed.sh` holding `vitest related --run "$@" && eslint --max-warnings=0 --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern "$@" && prettier --check --ignore-unknown "$@"`:

    "bkit:gate:changed": "sh scripts/gate-changed.sh"

`vitest related` finds only importers; also run the tests that read a changed file by its path (a text search of the test files for each path). The orchestrator's group gate, pre-push and CI still run the whole gates. To keep the whole gate on every change, add `gate-changed-script-missing` to `bkit.advisories.ignore` in package.json.

Gate contents (`.bkit/workflows.md` § Local gate scripts): every gate but `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration-e2e` and `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration-e2e-live` runs on a push or inside `/bkit-build`, so it MUST NOT run tests that need a deployed boundary or remote service; local services (a database in Docker) are fine.

--- 5/11 [advisory] gh-mcp-token-unset-shell ---
Detect: BKIT_GH_TOKEN is not set in the shell environment (undefined). The GitHub MCP server authenticates with `Authorization: Bearer ${BKIT_GH_TOKEN}` — without it, every tracker, PR, and board MCP call fails to connect.
Action: Set BKIT_GH_TOKEN in .bkit/.env (canonical local-secrets file, gitignored), then `direnv allow` and restart your editor so MCP servers pick it up:

    cp .bkit/.env.example .bkit/.env       # if not already done
    # edit .bkit/.env — set BKIT_GH_TOKEN=<PAT>
    direnv allow

Use a fine-grained PAT when every target repo sits under one owner (Contents, Pull requests, Issues, and Actions read & write, plus organization-scoped Projects read & write if you use board sync); use a classic PAT when one token must span owners (scopes repo / workflow / read:org / project / security_events). Generate at: https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens (fine-grained) or https://github.com/settings/tokens (classic). In cloud sessions (Claude Code web / Cursor Cloud Agents / Codex Cloud) set BKIT_GH_TOKEN in the dashboard env vars instead — repo files are not read for secrets there.

--- 6/11 [advisory] tracker-setup-github ---
Detect: bkit tracker is configured as `github`. GitHub Issues + Projects v2 is the active tracker.
Action: GitHub tracker: the GitHub MCP server authenticates with `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT for one owner, classic PAT across owners) — set it in `.bkit/.env`, then `direnv allow`. Unset → every tracker and PR MCP call fails. The `gh` CLI signs in separately: run `gh auth login` once. Ensure the `github` MCP server is configured in `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`.

--- 7/11 [advisory] github-project-board-sync-unconfigured ---
Detect: GitHub tracker is active but Projects v2 board status sync is not fully configured: `bkit.tracker.github.project` is empty or absent in package.json. Board sync silently no-ops — workflows never reflect phase on the project board.
Action: Board status sync is optional (workflows never gate on it) but invisible when half-configured. All three prerequisites are required:

1. Add the board's URL to package.json, as the browser shows it on the board (`/orgs/<org>/…` for an organization board, `/users/<login>/…` for a personal one; a trailing `/views/<n>` is fine):

       "bkit": {
         "tracker": {
           "github": { "project": "https://github.com/orgs/<org>/projects/<number>" }
         }
       }

   Workflows set the board's Status field by option name: `In progress` when a phase starts, `In review` at hand-off. A board whose Status options are named differently sets `"progress"` and `"review"` beside `"project"` to its own names.

2. Ensure the root `.mcp.json` github server enables the `projects` toolset:

       "X-MCP-Toolsets": "context,issues,pull_requests,repos,users,projects,actions"

3. The `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` PAT needs Projects read & write (repo scope is not enough): a fine-grained PAT gets it as an organization permission, so it reaches organization boards only; a classic PAT with the `project` scope reaches organization and personal boards.

To opt out and silence this advisory, set `bkit.tracker.github.project` to `false` in package.json.

--- 8/11 [advisory] cloud-secrets-three-locations ---
Detect: The secrets bkit's cloud integration uses must also be set in each cloud location you use. Bkit cannot verify dashboard state — surface the checklist so you don't ship a half-configured cloud setup.
Action: Set each secret in the required locations:

1. **Claude Code (web)**: open `https://claude.ai/code` → environment selector → your environment → **Environment variables**. Paste the block from `.claude/bkit-cloud.md` (gitignored), which also carries the setup script and network list. Claude reads both from the dashboard, NOT from the repo, so changes here do not require a commit.

**Context-fetch (`/bkit-debug` in the cloud):** if you run the debug workflow in these cloud agents, the observability creds your `.agents/context.md` context-fetch blocks use (e.g. `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`) must ALSO be set in the same dashboards above — non-interactively, since headless agents cannot `vercel login`. These are operator/observability READ creds, not app-runtime secrets. Commit the non-secret selectors (team scope / project ref / `--environment`) in your copied block so they need no dashboard entry. The CLIs those blocks call install automatically in the cloud from each block's `context-fetch:provision` sibling — no manual setup.

Same VALUE in all places.

--- 9/11 [advisory] project-docs-missing ---
Detect: No project document covers: docs/components.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/technology.md, docs/security.md, docs/data-schema.md, docs/testing.md, docs/deployments.md, docs/observability.md, docs/design.md, docs/noise.md, docs/setup.md.
Action: Copy the starter for each topic you want from `.bkit/templates/docs/` into `docs/`, fill it in from the repository, and add its row to `## Project Documents` in .agents/docs.md. A document you already keep elsewhere counts: index it with `Equivalent to <recommended path>` in its Scope cell. Skip topics that do not apply. Fill the docs in the order of .bkit/templates.md § Project docs — adoption order.

--- 10/11 [advisory] vale-package-not-synced ---
Detect: vale is on PATH but the repo has no .vale.ini and .vale/styles/write-good/ is absent — prose linting does not run.
Action: Adopt bkit's Vale template first: copy .bkit/templates/.vale.ini to .vale.ini and .bkit/templates/.vale/styles/Bkit/*.yml to .vale/styles/Bkit/. Then run `vale sync` (one-time per repo) to download the write-good package the copied .vale.ini names. `vale sync` reads its package list from .vale.ini, so it cannot fetch write-good before that file exists.

--- 11/11 [advisory] mcp-env-missing-dotenv ---
Detect: .bkit/.env.example exists but .bkit/.env does not. MCP servers and agent tooling will not have access to BKIT_GH_TOKEN.
Action: [mcp-env] Copy .bkit/.env.example to .bkit/.env and fill in your tokens (BKIT_GH_TOKEN) — in a git worktree, copy the main checkout's .bkit/.env instead, or run `bkit worktrees setup` to link it. Then run `direnv allow` to auto-export them into your shell. .bkit/.env is gitignored and safe to commit-skip.

--- Setup tips ---
Things not set up yet, most useful first. For the person: each tip says what goes wrong today and a sentence to ask your agent. For an AI agent: follow each tip's Agent steps unless the person declines it. Silence a tip by adding its id to `bkit.advisories.ignore` in package.json; `bkit-upgrade` cannot be silenced. Full template catalogue: .bkit/templates.md.

1. Give bkit its GitHub token (gh-mcp)
   You chose GitHub as your tracker, but bkit has no GitHub token, so every attempt to read an issue or open a pull request will fail. Add the token.
   Why: Choosing GitHub only tells bkit where your issues live. The token is what lets it actually sign in. Without it the setting looks right but nothing works, which is confusing to track down.
   Ask your agent: "Add my GitHub token as `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` in .bkit/.env, check .mcp.json has the `github` server, then run `direnv allow` and tell me to restart the editor."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/install.md` § Local env setup. The `github` server entry belongs in `.mcp.json` / `.cursor/mcp.json` (`.bkit/cloud.md` § MCP issue-tracker integration).

2. Create bkit's private settings file (bkit-env)
   bkit's private settings file (.bkit/.env) is missing or has blank entries, so nothing that needs to sign in can. Create it and fill it in.
   Why: This one file holds the sign-in tokens every bkit tool reads. It's never shared or committed. Most other tips depend on it, so do this one early.
   Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/.env.example to .bkit/.env and tell me which values I need to fill in."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/install.md` § Local env setup.

3. Let agents look code up directly (serena)
   Agents are finding code by searching for words, which is slower, costs more, and misses things. Set up Serena so they can look code up directly.
   Why: Serena lets agents look up code the way your editor does ("where is this defined, and what uses it?") instead of guessing from text search and reading whole files. That means fewer accidental changes, fewer rounds of you correcting them, and lower running costs because they read less. It can only look things up, never change your files.
   Ask your agent: "Run `brew install uv` and `uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent`, copy .bkit/templates/.serena/project.yml to .serena/project.yml and .bkit/templates/scripts/serena/ to scripts/serena/, then add the `serena` server from scripts/serena/bkit-serena.mcp.json to .mcp.json (details: .bkit/templates.md § Serena)."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Serena.

4. Automatic checks on every change (ci-workflow)
   Nothing checks your changes automatically before they're merged, so broken code can land unnoticed. Add bkit's check workflow.
   Why: This runs your tests and checks on GitHub every time something changes, and bkit's ship step waits for it to pass before merging. Without it, "shipped" only means "merged", not "checked".
   Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml to .github/workflows/<the file package.json `bkit.testing.ciWorkflow` names; default bkit-ci.yml>, replace `main` and `{{NODE_VERSION}}` in it with my default branch and Node major version, and add the `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `bkit:lint:prose`, `bkit:slop:delta` and `test` scripts to package.json as listed in .bkit/templates.md § Gate tool scripts."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § CI workflow and § Gate tool scripts.

5. Catch problems before they leave your machine (husky)
   Mistakes are only caught after changes reach GitHub. Add the local checks so they're caught the moment a change is saved to git.
   Why: These run the same checks on your own computer, in seconds, whenever a change is committed or pushed. Without them you find out minutes later from a failed build, after the agent has moved on and fixing it costs more.
   Ask your agent: "Run `pnpm add -D husky`, add `"prepare": "husky"` to the package.json scripts, copy .bkit/templates/.husky/pre-commit and .bkit/templates/.husky/pre-push to .husky/, and run `chmod +x .husky/pre-commit .husky/pre-push`."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Git hooks.

6. Consistent formatting (prettier)
   There's no shared formatting setup, so reviews fill up with spacing changes that hide the real ones. Add Prettier with bkit's ignore file.
   Why: Prettier (a code formatter) makes every file follow the same layout. bkit's ignore file stops it reformatting bkit's own files, which would otherwise show up as false changes every time bkit updates.
   Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/templates/prettierignore.example to .prettierignore first, then run `pnpm add -D prettier` and add `"format:check": "prettier --check ."` to the package.json scripts."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Prettier.

7. Catch junk code (slop-scan)
   Nothing catches the junk code AI tends to write. Add slop-scan so new junk gets flagged before it's merged.
   Why: Filler and dead code look fine when you skim a change, so they pile up unnoticed until the codebase is hard to trust. slop-scan flags only new problems, so it won't bury you in old ones.
   Ask your agent: "Run `pnpm add -D slop-scan`, copy .bkit/templates/slop-scan.config.json to slop-scan.config.json and .bkit/templates/scripts/slop/ to scripts/slop/, and add `"lint:slop": "slop-scan scan ."` and `"bkit:slop:delta": "bkit ci slop"` to the package.json scripts."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § slop-scan.

8. Keep written docs tight (vale)
   Nothing checks the project's written docs, so they slowly fill with vague, padded wording that agents then have to read. Add Vale.
   Why: Agents read your docs and instructions on every run. Padded writing costs time and money every time it's read, and vague rules get followed vaguely. Vale (a writing checker) flags it.
   Ask your agent: "Run `brew install vale`, copy .bkit/templates/.vale.ini to .vale.ini and .bkit/templates/.vale/styles/Bkit/ to .vale/styles/Bkit/, then run `vale sync`."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Vale.

9. Quick tidy-up on commit (lint-staged)
   The commit check has nothing to run. Add lint-staged so it tidies just the files you're committing.
   Why: It formats only the handful of files in each change, in about a second. Without it the commit check either does nothing or is slow enough that people start skipping it.
   Ask your agent: "Run `pnpm add -D lint-staged prettier` and copy .bkit/templates/lintstagedrc.example.json to .lintstagedrc.json."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § lint-staged.

10. Let debugging see real errors (context-fetch)
   When something breaks, the debug workflow can't see your live error reports or logs, so it has to guess from the code. Connect the services you use.
   Why: This lets /bkit-debug read the actual errors from your error tracker, hosting and database. Without it the agent works from guesses, and real problems stay hidden because nothing brings in the evidence.
   Ask your agent: "Copy the blocks for the services this project uses from .bkit/templates/context/ into .agents/context.md, below the `<!-- bkit:end -->` line, then tell me which tokens to add to .bkit/.env."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Context-fetch blocks.

11. Keep passwords the same everywhere (secrets-sync)
   Your deployment passwords are updated by hand in each service. Add bkit's sync tool so they're set in one place and copied everywhere.
   Why: The same password usually lives in several places: your hosting, your database, GitHub. When one falls out of step you get "works for me, broken in production", the slowest kind of bug to find. This keeps them matching and proves it without showing any values.
   Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/templates/scripts/secrets/ to scripts/secrets/, fill in scripts/secrets/bkit-secrets.config.mjs for the services this project uses, then run `node scripts/secrets/bkit-secrets.mjs sync --dry-run`."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Secrets sync.

12. Summarise long sessions earlier (compaction-window)
   Long sessions only summarise themselves when they're nearly full, so every step re-reads a huge history, and that re-reading is most of what a run costs. Set an earlier summarise point.
   Why: Each request re-reads the whole session so far. Left at the default, a session grows close to the model's full size before it summarises, and most subagents never summarise at all. An earlier summarise point keeps every request smaller.
   Caution: Summaries lose some detail. A summarise point set too low can stop agents mid-run. 300,000 tokens is a starting value, not yet checked on a real build.
   Ask your agent: "Add `"autoCompactWindow": 300000` to .claude/settings.json. For Codex, add `model_auto_compact_token_limit = 300000` at the top of .codex/config.toml, above the first `[section]`."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/providers.md` § Context compaction. Claude Code: `"autoCompactWindow": 300000` in `.claude/settings.json`. Codex: `model_auto_compact_token_limit = 300000` in `.codex/config.toml`, above the first `[section]` header.

13. Stop loading claude.ai connectors in this project (claude-connectors)
   Claude Code loads every connector on your claude.ai account in this project (for example email, calendar or file storage) and sends their names with every request, even when unused. If agents here don't use them, switch them off for this project.
   Why: Every connector's tool names are re-sent on every request, which is the largest part of the starting load you can remove. The connectors keep working in ordinary Claude chats (web and desktop app) and in cloud routines; only Claude Code in this project stops loading them.
   Ask your agent: "Check whether agents in this project use any claude.ai connectors. If none, add `"disableClaudeAiConnectors": true` to .claude/settings.json."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/providers.md` § claude.ai connectors. Move anything agents use through a connector onto the project's MCP file first, then set `"disableClaudeAiConnectors": true` in `.claude/settings.json`.

14. Issue forms (issue-forms)
   Optional: add issue forms so every new issue asks for what the agent reads first.
   Why: Each workflow starts from the issue. A form for an idea, a well-defined change or a bug asks for the problem, what done looks like, or the steps to reproduce. Without one, issues often arrive as a title and a line, and the agent has to guess.
   Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/templates/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ to .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ and commit it to the default branch."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Issue forms.

15. A map of the code (graphify)
   Optional: add graphify to keep an up-to-date map of how your code fits together.
   Why: With a map, agents check what already exists before building it again. Without one, agents and reviews work out the structure from scratch each time. That's slower, and it's easy to miss how one change ripples into another part of the code.
   Ask your agent: "Run `uv tool install "graphifyy[sql]"`, copy .bkit/templates/scripts/graphify/ to scripts/graphify/ and .bkit/templates/.graphifyignore to .graphifyignore, then add the graph scripts to package.json as listed in .bkit/templates.md § graphify."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § graphify.

16. Project docs (project-docs)
   Fill the project docs in waves, because each doc reads facts the earlier ones record.
   Why: Agents read your architecture, testing and security docs before they plan and build. A doc that is missing or still holds the starter text gives them nothing to go on, so they guess from the code each time.
   Caution: Ignoring either the missing-doc advisory or the unfilled-doc advisory also silences this tip and the other advisory.
   Ask your agent: "Fill in my project docs in the order of .bkit/templates.md § Project docs — adoption order: copy each missing starter from .bkit/templates/docs/ to docs/, fill it from the repository, and add its row to .agents/docs.md."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Project docs — adoption order.

17. Project goals (project-goals)
   Agents have rules but no goals, so when two options both fit the rules they choose by guesswork. Write down what this project optimises for.
   Why: Design and plan agents choose between options on every run. The rules say what is allowed, not what matters most here, so each agent weighs speed, cost and polish its own way.
   Ask your agent: "Fill the `## Project Goals` section that already exists in .agents/rules.md instead of adding a second one, with a few goals in priority order. Ask me what this project optimises for first."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/prompts.md` § Special Behaviors, where the Project Goals row sits.

18. Readable table changes (prettier-tables)
   Optional: if your docs have tables, add this so editing one cell doesn't show the whole table as changed.
   Why: Changing one cell normally reformats the whole table, so a one-word edit looks like a page of changes and reviewers can't see what actually moved.
   Ask your agent: "Copy .bkit/templates/scripts/prettier/bkit-insert-ignore.mjs to scripts/prettier/ and run `node scripts/prettier/bkit-insert-ignore.mjs`."
   Agent steps: `.bkit/templates.md` § Prettier tables.
